hyps: A Republican strategy to oppose Obama’s re-election
Republican leaders justify their policies by saying that they must fight election fraud.
However, the Brennan Center believes that voter fraud in the United States is less common than the number of people killed by lightning.
The Republican lawyers in the US have only recorded 300 cases of election fraud in 10 years.
One thing is certain: these new rules will have a negative impact on voter turnout.
In this sense, these measures undermine the democratic system of the United States.
Unlike Canada, the US states are responsible for conducting elections in their states.
In this sense, the majority of American governments have announced new laws since 2009 that make it more difficult to register or vote by mail.
This phenomenon has gained in importance since the elections of November 2010, when 675 new Republican representatives were elected in 26 states.
Instead, 180 bills were introduced in 2011 alone that would restrict voting rights in 41 states.
The new election laws require voters to present a photo ID and proof of US citizenship.
In addition, these laws also shorten the periods for early voting, make it illegal to register as a voter on election day, and deny the right to vote to citizens for whom there is a court order.
Prior to the 2006 elections, no US state required voters to show a photo ID.
Indiana was the first state to make such a demand.
The Supreme Court of the United States upheld the constitutionality of the Indiana law in 2008.
Republican authorities rushed to extend this practice to other states.
Over the past two years, they have promoted legislation in 34 states that requires voters to show a photo ID.
It is important to note that unlike Quebec, US citizens do not have a universal ID card like the health insurance card.
In fact, 11% of US citizens, or 21 million eligible voters, do not have a photo ID issued by a state government.
Moreover, five million new voters in 2012 will not have such an ID card.
However, it is often more than $100 to obtain the required ID.
The new restrictions are disproportionately affecting young people, minorities and low-income people.
In fact, 25% of African Americans, 15% of people earning less than $35,000, 18% of citizens over 65, and 20% of voters between 18 and 29 do not have the required photo ID.
This goes further.
Students who are considered voters, who vote for democratic candidates, are not allowed to use their student ID card in several states.
On the other hand, the same states allow members of hunting or fishing clubs to use the cards issued by these clubs for voting in elections.
Before 2004, no state required proof of citizenship to vote.
Arizona was the first state to introduce such a requirement.
Since 2011, a dozen states have passed laws requiring voters to prove they are U.S. citizens.
These measures are clearly aimed at limiting the voices of the Spanish.
For it is clear that two out of three Spanish voters prefer the Democratic Party.
In addition, Republican lawmakers in eight states in 2011 passed laws that eliminated voter registration on Election Day.
In addition, you have the right to restrict the ability of individuals and groups to provide assistance to voters who wish to register.
These restrictions have consequences.
For example, the voter registration campaigns for the general elections in 2004 helped to register approximately 10 million citizens.
Indeed, the proportion of new voters registered in 2010 was 17% lower than in 2006.
In addition, Republican lawmakers in five other states have passed legislation aimed at shortening the period for early voting.
For example, in the 2008 general election in Florida, 33% of voters who had voted early were African American, even though they make up only 13% of the state’s voters.
The same applies to the Hispanic population.
The latter made up only 11% of voters, but 24% of citizens who had voted in advance.
In contrast, the Whites, who represented 76% of voters, made up only 46% of voters who voted in advance.
Of course, democratic legislators and their supporters have been vigorous in opposing laws that restrict voter registration.
Several bills have been blocked by the vetoes of the democratic governors.
The US Attorney General intervened to suspend the most controversial laws.
They were able to limit the damage.
For example, only 16 of the 34 states have laws requiring the presentation of a photo ID.
However, the new rules introduced in 2012 will undoubtedly make it more difficult to exercise the right to vote.
The democratic critics denounce the party-political nature of the laws adopted and see in them a clear aim to influence the results in the countries that will be decisive in 2012.
A 2011 report from the Brennan Center shows that the states that have enacted these laws make up 171 of the 270 votes needed to win the presidency.
It is too early to say with certainty that these changes to the electoral system will have a significant impact on the outcome of the presidential elections in 2012.
But one thing is certain: these new rules will have a negative impact on voter turnout.
In this sense, these measures undermine the democratic system of the United States.
Prostate cancer screening: should the test be done or not?
The PSA test sometimes gives false results, with false negative or false positive results that lead to unnecessary medical procedures.
This leads to greater reluctance on the part of men who are already reluctant to undergo screening.
Should the test be done or not?
We have asked the opinion of two doctors.
The studies conducted in the US have been plagued by many confounding factors, making it difficult to interpret the data and make clear recommendations.
Another study, this time from Europe, concluded that there is a difference in mortality between patients with and without early detection.
This study also showed that after 12 years, the risk of developing metastases is 30 to 40% higher if no early detection was performed.
Therefore, I recommend the test from the age of 50 years or 40 years if you have a direct relative who has already been diagnosed with prostate cancer.
There is also a higher risk for men of African American heritage.
The most important thing is to make the right decision as soon as a cancer diagnosis has been made.
There are cancers that are aggressive and others that are indolent.

Patients must be made to understand the extent of the risk of their cancer, by showing them the possible options for prostate cancer that can be left untreated if it does not affect their quality of life in the long term, and in these cases we should opt for active monitoring of the disease.
Today, many men who have been diagnosed with cancer are not treated because their cancer is not aggressive and does not pose a threat to their lives.
It is suggested that they should be monitored actively and treated when the disease progresses.
As we become more precise in determining who should be treated and who should not,
Therefore, I still recommend that the test be carried out.
The most important thing is to talk to your doctor to determine whether it should be done or not.
In collaboration with the International Society of Urology, Movember has developed a tool that allows you to assess the pros and cons of the PSA test.
This document (currently only in English, but a translation will be available soon) can be downloaded at the following address: http://ca.movember.com/fr/mens-health/prostate-cancer-screening
Preventing the disease
Unfortunately, there is no magic bullet to prevent cancer.
Despite the advances in research, the best way to reduce the risk of developing it is to adopt a healthy lifestyle.
It is estimated that 30% of cancers could be prevented if everyone ate well and exercised enough.
"If there were no smokers, this value would increase at least to 50%," says André Beaulieu, spokesperson for the Canadian Cancer Society.
However, it is assumed that about 10% of cancer cases are caused by heredity.
Several remain completely unresolved.
For the Canadian Cancer Society, the fight against tobacco dependence remains a priority, despite the decline in the number of smokers.
Smoking is responsible for 85% of lung cancer cases.
It is also a risk factor for several other cancers.
It seriously damages people’s health.
"Today there are still 1.5 million smokers in Quebec," laments spokesman André Beaulieu.
Encouraging data: 10 years after quitting smoking, the risk of dying from cancer is reduced by half.
The weight
According to the Canadian Cancer Society, obesity and adiposity also promote the onset of the disease.
They appear to increase the risk of breast, colon, rectal, esophageal, pancreatic, and uterine cancers.
"Research shows that regular physical activity throughout life protects against colon cancer," he adds.
The food
The organization also recommends limiting consumption of red meat.
In large quantities it increases the risk of developing a cancer of the rectum or the colon.
Sausage should also be avoided.
The preservation of meat by smoking, drying or salting can lead to the formation of carcinogens.
"These can damage the body cells and lead to the development of cancer," he explains.
Vitamins
In recent years, several scientists have investigated the relationship between vitamin supplements and cancer.
But your research is not yet conclusive.
According to the Canadian Cancer Society, the studies on vitamin E are contradictory.
While one study found a reduction in the risk of prostate cancer, another showed an increase.
The effect of vitamin D on cancer has not yet been clearly demonstrated.
Mr Beaulieu also stresses the importance of talking to your doctor about your concerns and your family history.
"Performing a screening test does not lead to cancer."
The Higgs boson analyses
The announcement of the possible discovery of the Higgs boson caused some excitement last summer, and for good reason.
It is believed that this boson is involved in nothing less than the mechanism that is responsible for the mass of all objects in the universe.

Finally, it is the last particle whose existence is predicted by the Standard Model - our best or "least wrong" explanation of nature and the behavior of matter - but which has not yet been observed empirically.
But for physicists it is not yet certain that it is really the Higgs boson.
We know without a shadow of a doubt that we have a real new particle, and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
Moreover, it seems to be confirmed by new data presented this week at a major physics conference in Kyoto, but there is still not enough data to be completely sure.
Let us assume, however, that it is indeed the Higgs, since there seems to be a very small risk of being mistaken, and let us see what it is all about.
There is an inevitable law in this world that prevents two objects from being present at the same place at the same time.
It is not possible to violate this rule - and try not to do so, because you will suffer.

For even though particle physics is a strange world, it turns out that it too is subject to a law: the Pauli exclusion principle, which states that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "quantum state," which is essentially a state of some of their properties.
On this basis, physicists divide particles into two categories.
In one corner are the good citizens, called Fermions, who obey the Pauli principle.
And in the other, the bosons move, a wicked band of anarchists who are not sacred to anything - in any case not the principle, which means that they can be at the same time at the same place.

These bosons are divided into two groups according to the Particle Adventure website from the Berkeley Laboratories (which is absolutely amazing) : the mesons, which we will not discuss here, and the "force particles" that spread the great forces of nature and with which the Higgs boson would somehow be related.
It must be stressed here, however, that these bosons are not all as exotic creatures as one might think.
If you are able to read this chronicle, it is only thanks to a boson of exceptional banality: the photon or the "particle of light" which is the "messenger" of the electromagnetic force.
If a particle with an electric charge is accelerated or changes direction, the electromagnetic field is disturbed exactly at that point, as if a pebble were thrown into a pond.
This "disturbance" creates an electromagnetic wave (light, infrared or ultraviolet radiation, etc.), and this wave is nothing other than a photon and therefore one of the bosons "carriers of force".
More stable field
The same is true of the Higgs boson, with the difference that another field, the Higgs field, must be "disturbed" in order for that boson to appear.
However, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field; the particle must reach very high energies, a little like a frozen pond that could only be pierced by a very large rock.
Therefore, a huge particle accelerator such as the LHC is needed to achieve such energies. The LHC is a ring with a circumference of 27 km!
The analogy with the electromagnetic field is again useful to explain the relationship between the Higgs and the mass.
It is not all particles and not all matter that interacts with the electromagnetic field.
Some, like magnets, do this, but others do not - for example, a sheet of paper will never hold itself to the refrigerator.
And similarly, not all particles interact with the Higgs field: those that do have a mass, while the others (like the photon) do not.
What good can all this research do, asks Mrs Plamondon?
For science, they are used to test the standard model (SM), and they also allow physicists to precisely examine all the discrepancies between the observations and the SM predictions.
There are many physicists who are eagerly awaiting such deviations, as the slightest difference could open a door to a "new physics" and could plug some of the holes in the model.
One must say that the latter still has major shortcomings, as it does not provide an explanation for gravity (ups!) and dark matter, which makes up about 80% of the matter in the universe (ups!).
However, no such deviations have been found at CERN to date.
Effects
The impact of these research on the general public is more difficult to predict, but it would be wrong to assume that there is none.
By the early 1960s, however, the pioneers of the laser in Bell Laboratories had no idea that their work would spark a revolution.
They saw scientific applications but nothing else.

In fact, the late physicist Willard Boyle - who worked at Bell Labs where the laser was invented in the 1960s and who himself developed the first continuous-wave laser (the first were pulsed) in 1962 - said that the laser was considered at first to be a "laboratory toy."
Imagine...
Moreover, applications can also arise from all the instruments that surround research.
For example, in 1969, while working on optics, Willard Boyle developed a small light sensor.
Although it was not the original purpose, this sensor today serves as the "eye" to all digital cameras around the world and has won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2009.
Of course, this does not mean that the activities of the LHC will necessarily change our lives, but it does mean that we will never know for sure...
Palliative care - the best way to die... | Le Devoir
Quebec's Committee on "Dying with Dignity" recently discussed the sensitive issue of end-of-life care.
The debate must be resumed shortly, even though a draft law is being prepared.
However, there is still much to be done in this important area.
The Devoir has tried to look at this more closely.
A few weeks ago, Mr L. was still living alone in his apartment in Montérégie.
The prostate cancer that had afflicted him had given him a two-year life expectancy.
"They gave me five years to live, I have achieved seven years", he said half-heartedly, lying in his bed in the Victor-Gadbois palliative care home in Beloeil where he arrived the day before.
"However, it is always a shock, you cannot prepare for it," he says.
The disease is doing its work: an immeasurable weakness prevents him from going to the toilet alone and even from eating on his own.
Sitting at the table before a delicious lunch, he reluctantly agrees to be helped with the meal.
Boldly he even manages to smile and talk to the strangers who are around him, bringing him his medicine and offering him a bath.
The courage of ordinary death.
"My greatest wish is that my diarrhea is cured, as this is humiliating," he says.
Some hours later the team has found a remedy for this evil.
"Over the course of our lives we learn that a man pees standing up," says Pierre Brodeur, psychologist at the Victor-Gadbois Home.
To go back to childhood is an unacceptable humiliation for some people.
"It depends on the person's ability to accept a setback," he says.
For several people working in palliative care, major events are taking place amid these setbacks.
The patients admitted to the Victor-Gadbois palliative care home are all suffering from cancer.
They have a maximum life expectancy of three months.
At this stage, they are no longer showered with so-called "healing" care by doctors and nurses.
For Mrs A., 89, the worst fear is to die "conscious and by suffocation".
But through the illness I have really come to know my children.
"I have good children," she adds.
"I have no more wishes in life," she says, before accepting that one puts a mask on her that helps her breathe.
You will still have a last visit from your son, who is coming from Italy.
At the Victor-Gadbois home, volunteers provide personal care and help with meals.
Palliative care is used when there are no other options.
To make dying more pleasant.
In Quebec, there is one bed for every 11,700 residents for palliative care.
That is very little when we consider that we will all die one day.
Here, life is continued under the best possible conditions, explains Dr. Christiane Martel, one of the doctors at the home.
Both in terms of physical, emotional or spiritual comfort.
The dying person is given a choice of mouth care with brandy or Pepsi.
The diabetic no longer has to check their blood sugar level.
And death is part of everyday life.
Last night we served a beer to Mr X who died during the night.
This morning his son will drink the beer at his father's feet.
"We help both patients and their families," says Nathalie Savard, Director of Nursing.
At the Victor-Gadbois Home, no day is like any other.

In addition to an old man of 93 years, who enjoys the last family reunion in the courtyard and is well supported by his pillows, while he is being honored, a young man of 36 years dies tragically, surrounded by his parents, his wife and his two small children, after having tried everything to survive.
"For six months, three to five beds have been occupied by cancer patients under the age of 45," Dr. Christiane Martel is worried.
53% of the patients admitted to the Victor-Gadbois Home come from their home, 47% come from the hospital.
The problem of access to palliative care

It is said that 77% of Canadians do not have access to palliative care, i. e. a care that aims to alleviate the suffering of patients when they have reached the end stage of their life, at home, in hospital or in a nursing home.
And several organizations, such as the Home Victor-Gadbois and the Society for Home Palliative Care in the Greater Montreal area specialize more or less exclusively in the care of cancer patients.
This very same lack of care in Quebec's health system is what is causing several palliative care specialists to be concerned about the adoption of a law regulating euthanasia and assisted suicide.

Since the month of October, a manifesto has been circulating signed by prominent figures in palliative care such as Dr. Balfour Mount and Dr. Bernard Lapointe to express their opposition to such an initiative.
According to Dr. Christiane Martel, Quebec's health system is not strong enough to ensure that everyone has the right to high quality palliative care before accepting euthanasia.
Recently, she says, I saw a patient who was in the emergency room for 14 days with severe pain, without any action taken to relieve it.
I fear that patients are dying because they do not receive adequate health care.
At the same time, several oncologists treat their patients with a fierce determination to the last day.
Hélène Richard’s chances of survival were already minimal when she stopped a grueling chemotherapy regimen.
When I told my oncologist that I was going to stop the treatment, she said that she was sorry that I was giving up the fight, she said.
However, she had told me that I was at the end!
No omnipotent care
Dr. Martel believes that 90% of patients who have asked to die are grateful to the nursing staff for not allowing them to die after their pain has been relieved by a team of palliative care.
It must be made clear, however, that palliative care is not omnipotent in pain management.
According to Elsie Monereau, head of palliative care at the Société de soins palliatifs du Grand Montréal, 8% of patients do not respond to pain treatment.
At the end of life, doctors often resort to terminal sedation, which consists of putting the patient to sleep either sporadically or permanently until the moment of death.
We cannot continue to pretend that we do not see this side of suffering.
Patients without pain relief will increasingly have the option of using this terminal sedation.
Patients who are not relieved of their pain say the same thing: "I want to die."
But it does not necessarily mean "I want you to put me to sleep" but "I want my pain to be relieved".
The realization of this report was possible thanks to a journalism scholarship from Canadian health research institutes.
Real estate scandals of great magnitude in Quebec

Officials of the road construction office, companies in the construction industry, money-makers for political parties and specialists of the Italian Mafia tell every day what they know about a great "system" in which construction industry, officials, politicians, trade unionists and mafiosi are involved.
An "industry" that was very expensive for Quebec taxpayers, especially in the 1990s and 2000s.
"It is strange how the system has collapsed since drastic measures have been taken," Jacques Duchesneau, a member of the National Assembly of Quebec and former police chief of Montreal, jokes.

The scandal was uncovered by him as a result of a thorough investigation of the misappropriation of funds related to contracts for road construction in Quebec, which the then Premier had only reluctantly agreed to.
The "Duchesneau report" established a direct link between industry, secret funding of parties and bribery of officials.

"Since the start of the investigation in 2010", he stresses, "the Ministry of Transport alone could have saved a billion dollars on contracts", because some were restraining their instinct to get their share!
The Charbonneau Commission "has already brought two mayors to justice," he adds, hoping that it will be able to "expose the tactics behind the individuals."
A permanent anti-corruption unit
The permanent anti-corruption unit, which was set up in 2011, is also making great efforts with its army of auditors, investigators and analysts in the government.
Also the police of the "Marteau-Truppe", which since 2009 has made the "sewage cartel" of Montreal more cautious in inflating contracts...
In recent weeks, she has conducted a series of raids and brought charges of fraud and corruption against local officials like Frank Tampino and Richard Marcotte, the mayor of a suburb.
The next on the list would be Gilles Vaillancourt, who just resigned as mayor of Laval, Quebec’s third-largest city.
He is suspected of having accepted bribes in exchange for public contracts.
The engineers of Montreal’s road construction office and Italian entrepreneurs such as Tony Accurso and Lino Zambito were specifically charged.
The latter has caused a stir by declaring to the Commission how the system works for obtaining public contracts.
He himself paid 3% of the value of the contracts he received in Montreal to a broker linked to the Mafia, who then transferred the money to the Union Montreal, the party of Mayor Gérald Tremblay.
Mr Zambito has been involved in the 2000s in all sorts of ways, having given more than $88,000 (approximately €68,000) to provincial parties, especially to the Liberals who were in power at the time.
He also admitted to having organized illegal funding for former Liberal Vice-President Nathalie Normandeau.
Sewerage contracts, whose costs he artificially inflated
In Montreal, the system of corruption worked smoothly.

The former civil engineer Gilles Surprenant has described this in detail to the Commission: over ten years he received gifts from the construction company, invitations to trips, golf tournaments, restaurants and ice hockey games, as well as bribes amounting to $736,000 in return for sewer contracts, whose costs he artificially inflated.
Other officials in the road construction office have admitted that they have been inflating the bills artificially by 30-40% by adding false extra services.
Furthermore, an organizer of the mayor's party, Martin Dumont, has accused Mr Tremblay of having deliberately ignored a shadow budget that was used to fill his coffers with black money.
As a result of these revelations, Mr Tremblay resigned in early November, plunging Montreal into a major crisis.
Chantal Rouleau was one of the first Montreal representatives to raise the alarm.

As mayor of the Rivière-des-Prairies borough, in the east of the island, she opposed the sale of a municipal property that was purchased for $5 million and sold for $1.6 million to a developer in the booming real estate market.
70% of black money in the election campaigns

The investigation that is ultimately carried out tells us that it is "pulling on a thread that allows us to understand how the system that has been subverted by ants works, so that we can stop the evil and denounce the guilty".
She says that the process is "painful but positive".
We are in the process of cleaning up the wound, but we would need a Montreal-specific investigation unit, as well as supervision to prevent a return of questionable practices.
How to clean.
Regularly.
Jacques Duchesneau, for his part, notes that "officials have stolen several hundred million dollars," but he is especially concerned about the role of "agents of the state who are in on the scam"
Starting from a 70% black economy in financing the election campaigns in Quebec, he jokes: "I was told that this was only a poor imitation of reality."

The Quebec government proposes to limit donations to parties to $100, which it says will not change the situation: "As long as campaign spending is not strictly limited, black money will continue to circulate in politics."

He recommends a complete overhaul of the system for awarding public contracts and funding the parties: "We cannot go any deeper; by going to the root of things with courage, we can rebuild the house on a more solid basis with more controls and laws."
If this story damages Quebec's and Montreal's international reputation, Mr Duchesneau calls on those who laugh at it to look in their own backyard...

With Bitcoin, you can pay and sell without a bank
The opposite of the current monetary exchange based on central banks, identified transactions and processing fees between the parties.
Moreover, as is often the case in these technologies, there is a political vision: the conviction that the current monetary system, dominated by bank monopolies, leads to financial crises.

In fact, the bitcoin invented by Satoshi Nakamoto (a pseudonym) is both a virtual currency (but convertible into dollars, euros, etc.) and a protocol for secure exchange like BitTorrent, which allows direct exchange of files.
With 15,000 computers in the network, approximately 200,000 transactions have already been recorded.
Some thousand websites accept Bitcoin as a donation or as a payment method.
After Bitcoin’s price peaked at $30 (23 euros) in June 2011, it fell to $2 five months later before recovering to around $10 today (prices are listed on bitcoincharts.com).
Nothing particularly impressive compared to world trade in real currencies or financial products.
However, the European Central Bank (ECB) has shown interest in this in a report published in October on virtual currencies.
It describes Bitcoin as "the most successful virtual currency", "in competition with the dollar or euro" and "similar to traditional currencies".
Bitcoin differs from other types of virtual currency like the "credits" used to advance in a video game, which can be won or purchased (and sometimes traded) by playing.
The social network Facebook has also developed a similar system.
However, trade is always controlled and processed by a central authority.
With Bitcoin, all nodes are simultaneously custodians, auditors, money-makers, and buyers and sellers.
How does this network work?
Each transaction between two users is actually between two e-mail addresses in the form of an e-mail.
With the difference that the user can choose a different address for each payment, which ensures anonymity.
A number of the data related to this transaction is signed electronically by a double encryption system.
In this way, the network can verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Using the contents of the file it is also possible to ensure that the bitcoins traded are present in the public ledger of accounts that is distributed throughout the network.
The crucial step is to record this new transaction in the book.
This is done through a mathematical problem that is started on the computers, where the winner, who is a sort of temporary central banker, has the privilege of adding that extra line.
It is a file fragmentation, i. e. the conversion of a large file into a shorter and unique electronic fingerprint.
The computer "takes" the new transaction and adds a number before it is "hacked"
The goal is to find the number that gives a special fingerprint (many zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the other nodes can easily check if it is the right one.
The transaction is thus permanently linked to the chain of all other transactions, and any modification would change the fingerprint.

If a user wants to defraud twice very quickly (less than 10 minutes) with the same money, only one of the two transactions would be validated by the network and the other would remain unlinked because both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solved the problem receives 50 bitcoins.
To prevent inflation, this reward is halved regularly, probably before the end of 2012.
The bitcoins in circulation are thus limited to 21 million, but divisible to one hundred millionth, which leaves some room for manoeuvre...
Moreover, the difficulty of the task is increased with each improvement in computing power.
The life of the network has already had highs and lows.
The websites that provide services for Bitcoin have been attacked and the Bitcoin deposits have been stolen.
"The vulnerability affects not the protocol itself," assures Pierre Noizat, who just launched Paymium, a company that accepts real money and uses the Bitcoin network.
The ECB also reports on the possibilities of money laundering using this anonymous service.
However, cash also has this deficiency.
Major players like Wikipedia have refused to accept such donations.
Others, such as the blog platform WordPress, accept them.
Recently, Adi Shamir and Dorit Ron from the Weizmann Institute in Israel analyzed the ledger and showed that almost 80% of the bitcoins are not in circulation.
In November, a "mega-liquidation" was launched.
"Thirty thousand dollars were exchanged," says Jon Holmquist, who works for Coinabul, a company that converts bitcoins into gold.
Pierre Noizat, who also wrote a book about this currency, believes strongly in the potential of this technology as a transaction network.
Its system Paytunia is a credit card (with real money) or contactless payment with a mobile phone, but uses Bitcoin to validate transactions, which are cheaper.
Moreover, the holder manages his identity and can thus remain anonymous.
The system can be easily implemented by the retailers, and they do not have to install new terminals or computer programs.
You just have to give an address that can be "photographed and recognized" by a phone, says Pierre Noizat, who claims to have thousands of users.
There is a general trend to review hierarchical systems in favour of more horizontal systems.
"It will take some time for Bitcoin to gain traction, but 2013 could be a turning point," he predicts.
The ECB's report, by the way, suggests that it will re-assess the various risks that today are considered to be high in the event of a success of this currency.
We have left Afghanistan.

NATO and the US should follow in late 2014.
It is time for the Afghan army to take back control of its territory, and for the Afghan people to decide their own future without expecting anything from us.
We have particularly punished the Afghan farmers by considering them to be terrorists.
And ourselves with our 88 soldiers killed, as well as the injured and wounded.
The Taliban are made up of foreign extremists, former leaders who fled to Pakistan, but also often of peasants who reject an armed foreign presence, as was the case during the Soviet occupation.
They want to defend their centuries-old and archaic traditions, even if they have been joined by jihadists, Pakistanis, Arabs, Uzbeks and Tajiks.
Tolerated, sometimes supported by local insurgents, they will not be there when the West becomes discreet.
The withdrawal of French troops from the base at Nijrab, which I observed from a hill planted with almond trees, financed by French loans, was carried out properly.
The convoys of trucks and tanks that were flown over by helicopters have reached Kabul without being attacked.
As of the end of 2014, there will be no more influx of Taliban into Kabul.
Since its irresistible march from 1994 to 1996, the conditions have changed.
At that time Kabul was empty and the country was under siege from the various insurgent groups.
Their takeover was seen as a kind of liberation and return to security.
The Afghan women have paid the price for the obscurantism of the farmers overwhelmed by the organization of Al-Qaida, but their situation has not improved to date.
Former mujahedin, the Afghan government and current Taliban have a common desire to keep women in a subordinate position.
The main personalities of the anti-Soviet war have returned to power in 2001.

They have transformed themselves into business people by seizing government land to sell to refugees from Iran and Pakistan as building land, taking advantage of the massive American subcontracting of construction.

As I have heard in the campaigns, people want a government that is not made up of thieves.

The private initiative is given priority.

The new cooperation agreement provides for the continuation of traditional aid: girls' and boys' schools, the Institute of French at the universities, the French Institute, cooperation in the military, legal, medical and agricultural fields, support for the archaeological delegation.

A much more modest budget will contribute to improving local living conditions, which are very hard in these valleys often located at more than 2000 meters.
The letter contains dozens of written inquiries from small-scale agricultural projects from the districts of Kapisa.

A constitution by the back door in Egypt
It is a new game of poker by President Mohammed Morsi.
While Egypt remains more divided than ever over the constitutional declaration that temporarily grants it unlimited authority, it has decided to go all in.
To everyone's surprise, he announced on Wednesday that the Constitutional Assembly would adopt its final version the next day.
Just a week ago, the President granted this House two additional months to complete its work.
Egypt has been operating under a provisional, repeatedly amended text for almost two years, which undermines institutional stability and creates a legal muddle.
This new initiative has only served to deepen the country's divisions.
For his opponents, the President is in his "autocratic delirium" by continuing to "break his word" and "trampling on the law".
On the side of its supporters, it is claimed that it is a way to end the institutional and political crisis as soon as possible and to accelerate the transition process.
Within 14 days a referendum should be held.
A very short period of time that forces the brothers to abandon their project to explain the text to the Egyptians, section by section.
For the President it is also a way of regaining his public and democratic legitimacy, while protests are raging across the country.
After assurances in an interview with the American weekly Time, it seems that Mohammed Morsi is convinced that Egyptians will vote for him.
In particular, the Egyptian people are being given an ultimatum: "Either you vote for my draft or I will retain unlimited authority," which is supposed to end after the constitution is adopted.
85 of the largely Islamist members of this Constituent Assembly approved the text yesterday in a strange atmosphere.
The majority of the Liberals have not complied with the call.
Just before the declaration of the Constitution in mid-November, they turned away because they felt they had not been able to express their views.
Representatives of human rights organizations, religious minorities or civil society have also acted in the same way.
In order to ensure quorum, 11 persons, substitute members, were added yesterday morning.
Some are very close to the Muslim Brotherhood.
It is not surprising that the articles were adopted by consensus.

The commentators found it amusing that the only disagreement of the day... was expressed at the time of prayer, as some members of the body thought that the pendulum clock of the Constituent Assembly was not running exactly.
The text, which was adopted last night, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, which attracted all the attention, is, after all, identical to that of the 1971 Constitution, stating that "the principles of Sharia are the main source of law".
The Salafist parties, who consider the establishment of Islamic law a major demand, had hoped to replace "principles" with "rules" which would have made a more rigorous application possible.
For the Islamists, the fact that this article has not been changed is proof of their good will and respect for the other members of Egyptian society.
"Hypocrisy" is the Liberal response, who see it only as a propaganda stunt.
For they argue that Islamization of the constitution occurs through other articles.
In particular, they are looking at Article 220, which recognises the University of Al-Azhar's advisory role, in particular in relation to the review of compliance with the laws of Sharia.
According to the Egyptian specialist Sophie Pommier, this is worrying because "the people called upon to comment are not elected and have no democratic legitimacy.
One can see here the first signs of a theocracy.
Liberal fears are also fuelled by the fact that the next rector of the university will be much less moderate than the current one.
"At present there is no clear religious commitment.
With this constitution we remain within the framework of the civil state.
Most of the lawyers who have worked on this text are not ulema, but academics, some of whom have been trained in the French system.
He acknowledges, however, that there may be ambiguity in relation to Article 220, given that the terms used are borrowed from the religious vocabulary.
This refers in particular to the "fiqh" [Islamic jurisprudence, ed. note].
And in the future the question may be asked as to whether civil judges are competent to decide.
In addition to its religious aspect, the text adopted yesterday is strongly criticised because of the wide powers it gives to the President of the Republic.
The Muslim Brotherhood argues that these are significantly reduced from the former regime.
Another point of contention: the army’s powers.
In line with the military's wish, the defence budget will not be presented to Parliament, but to a national defence council.
There will be no ban on civil proceedings in military courts, as the human rights organisations have called for.
The latter also share their concerns about the text, which they consider to be a threat to freedom.
The blasphemy law will be maintained, and insults are now banned, which could have serious consequences for the right to freedom of expression, especially for the press.
Moreover, no article now refers to the protection of women, says Heba Morayef of Human Rights Watch.
In your opinion, the only positive point is the prohibition of torture by Article 36.
This word was not included in the previous Constitution.
While the Egyptian President was forced to speak on television last night, demonstrations are planned for this afternoon.
The supporters of the head of state will march on Saturday.
In Israel, Ukrainian tourists will find holy places, the navel of the world and a sea of salt
The Promised Land combines the beauty of biblical truths, modern comforts and untouched nature.
AIF gives you the five main reasons to visit Israel.
Before the sacred places,
Visit the River Jordan, where Jesus was baptized.
It is said that all who bathe in this river receive God's blessing.
Galilee is the place where Jesus performed his miracles: the transformation of water into wine at a wedding, walking on water, the calming of the sea storm and the fishing.
Here, Jesus appeared to his disciples after the resurrection.
Most of the holy sites, however, are located in Jerusalem.
Here, the faithful walk the Way of the Cross (in Latin: Via Dolorosa).

The route begins at the Roman fortress of Antonia, the pretorium, where the court was, and continues through the streets of the old town to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre on Mount Calvary, where the place of the Crucifixion, the Stone of Unction and the tomb of Jesus are located.
Here is the navel of the world, which is the symbol of the salvation of humanity.
The Church of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem is located on the site where, according to a Christian legend, the tree grew from which the cross was made for the crucifixion of Jesus.
Jerusalem is also the holiest place for the Jews - the Western Wall, the remains of a temple destroyed by the Romans in 70 AD.
It is a tradition for people of different faiths to leave notes with their wishes, which are then fulfilled.
A trip to the heights
The ruins of the fortress of Masada are the remains of the secret refuge built by Herod the Great in 25 AD for his family.
They are located on a cliff in the mountains at 450 meters above sea level.
Only hikers can reach the ruins on their own.
All the others are brought by a cable car to this historic summit.
In the north of the country at an altitude of 1600 to 2040 meters is the famous ski area Hermon, which attracts countless tourists in winter months.
From the foot of the mountain you can get there by shuttle bus.
The ski slopes have a total length of 45 kilometres.
According to an old legend, the mountain peak was the home of pagan gods.
Unique museums visit
There are almost 300 museums in this country.
In one trip you can not see all of them.
But at least the five most interesting should be visited.
One of these is the Israel Museum, which is close to the Knesset (Parliament).
There are also some 500,000 archaeological and anthropological exhibits, including the Dead Sea Scrolls, housed in the museum.
The Museum of Art in Tel Aviv is also worth a visit.
There are collections of Impressionist and Expressionist works by Monet, Pissarro, Renoir, Cézanne, Sisley, Matisse, Modigliani, Chagall and Picasso.
In Akko you can visit the Museum in the Bath of Al Basha, which houses several rooms of ancient Turkish baths with sculptures of the visitors and bath attendants.
In Caesarea you should visit the unique private Ralli Museum where you can admire sculptures by Dali and Rodin.
There are no guides or souvenir shops.
Admission is free, and donations are not accepted.
The fifth museum, the Holocaust Museum in Tel Aviv, tells one of the most shocking chapters in history.
The most poignant section is the memorial to the children, built to commemorate the 1.5 million children who were murdered in the concentration camps and gas chambers.
When you enter the room, it is completely dark.
Stars shine.
And it is the names of the Jewish children and the countries in which they died.
Ukraine is also mentioned.
Something for health
The three main areas for relaxation in Israel are located on the shores of the Mediterranean, the Red Sea and the Dead Sea.
At each of the three locations there are swimming pools, water parks, dolphinariums and aquariums.
Surprisingly, the Red Sea is also bathed in the winter months, as the water temperature does not fall below 21 °C and the air warms up to 23 °C.
The Dead Sea is even warmer and people bathe there all year round.
By the way, this unusual sea with a depth of 417 meters below sea level is the deepest sea in the world.
Its turquoise water is high in salt content and is safe for non-swimmers to walk on.
The surrounding countryside is simply beautiful.

Visitors come here for treatments using salt water (natural salt licks) and healing mud as well as for the treatment of skin infections, allergies, asthma, eczema, arthritis, bronchitis, diabetes and to calm over-stressed nerves.
The secrets of the ancient world touch
These secrets are hidden in the Old City of Tel Aviv, namely the city of Jaffa on the Mediterranean coast.
This city was the site of a famous waterway that connected Egypt, Syria, Anatolia, and Mesopotamia.
The city is mentioned in ancient Greek and Egyptian legends.
According to tradition, Noah was building his ark here, and Perseus rescued the beautiful Andromeda, with whom he lived a long and happy life in this place.
Tourists like to stroll through the narrow streets named after the zodiac signs.
Fortune is said to be kind to all who touch the walls in the alley with their star sign.
In Jaffa you can find newlywed couples from all over Israel and even from other countries at photo sessions.
In Caesarea, the city of King Herod, you can stroll through the Roman Theater and conquer the fortress of the Crusaders.
In Roman times Caesarea was the most important city in Judea and the residence of the Roman governors, including Pontius Pilate.
The carefully restored theatre is now used for evening concerts and operas.
Tourist's wish list
If you are going to Israel, do not worry about your poor English: about 30% of Israelis speak Russian.
The money in the trip is preferred to take in dollars, which can be easily exchanged for shekels (current exchange rate: 1 dollar to 3.8 shekels).

In the city you usually get around by bus, but in Jerusalem there is also a light rail and in Haifa the only metro line in the country with six stations that connects the lower city with the upper city.
In fact, it is an underground cable car.
A ride within the city costs 6 shekels, which includes transfers for a ride of up to 1.5 hours.
According to Jewish tradition, the Sabbath is observed in Israel on Saturday.
From Friday evening to sunset on Saturday, markets and shops are closed, and public transport is suspended.
And on Sunday morning begins the working week.
In many cafes, restaurants and restaurants only kosher food is served, which excludes pork, seafood, fish without scales and food that contains both dairy and meat products.

Instead, you have the choice between different dishes with ham and beef, soups and desserts (prepared with coconut milk), traditional Jewish hummus paste, different sauces, fried balls made of mashed beans and peas (falafel) and fruits and vegetables.
There are no stray dogs in the streets of Israeli cities.
There are many well-fed cats roaming the streets, free to roam and play.
In the evening, you can even see them sleeping on the roofs of parked cars.
Cats like lively places and are not averse to treats.
A rental car will cost between $37 per day (Hyundai Getz) and $188 per day (Audi A6, Volvo S80).
The insurance costs an additional $15 per day.
And bicycle rental costs 15 shekels per day.
Entrance tickets to museums cost on average 30 shekels.
In numbers
In 2012, more than three million tourists from around the world visited Israel.
Most of the adventurers and tourists came from Russia, France, Germany, Italy, England, the USA and Ukraine.

From January to October 2012, 118,8 thousand Ukrainian tourists visited the Holy Land, which is an increase of 51% compared to the same period in 2010, before the visa-free regime was lifted on 9 February 2011.
"The great and mighty" leads to Moscow: Migrants save money for language
While Members of Parliament and civil rights activists debate the benefits of the mandatory language tests for migrants, criminals are already trading in forged certificates
Every year, 13 million guest workers come to Moscow, St. Petersburg and other cities in Russia.
Most of them are the citizens of Central Asia: Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
Their sole purpose is to earn money to support their families back home.
On 1 December, a law came into force requiring all migrant workers to take a test certifying their knowledge of Russian.
So far, this rule applies only to migrants who want to work in the service sector, in the housing sector and in retail.
However, the tests are to become mandatory for all guest workers in the future, according to the Federal Migration Office.
In addition to language tests, students must also take tests on Russian history and the basics of law.
Language skills must be demonstrated both for the acquisition and extension of the work permit.
Exceptions apply only to citizens of countries where Russian is an official language.
Also exempt from this law are people who received their diplomas and certificates before the collapse of the USSR in 1991.
Purpose, the issues and protection of rights

The whole of the testing centres will be under the aegis of the Pushkin Institute for Russian Language, the Russian State University for the Humanities, the Moscow State University, the St. Petersburg State University and other Russian universities.
Migrants can take the tests in any city; already more than 160 such centres have been opened in Russia.
The initiative to introduce the tests was supported by the Members of the State Duma and the Federal Migration Service.
Civil rights activists, however, asked in the press several times before the law came into force: what is the point of all this?
What changes does the requirement to have language skills bring for both Russians and guest workers?
In particular, the spokesman for the Migration Office said that the aim was to reduce the number of forced labourers.
"Many are now talking about protecting the rights of migrant workers," says Viktor Sebelew, head of the Federal Migration Service's representation in Tajikistan.
However, your rights must be protected before you leave.
Only an organized recruitment will solve 90% of the problems of foreign workers.
Migrants without a profession, education, language skills and medical examination are faced with problems.

Sebelew believes that a future migrant without language skills will inevitably encounter people with evil intentions who will put him in a dark, cramped tent, where he will have to wait months without food and documents and work 12 to 14 hours a day.
We receive many complaints from our migrants.

"At home they promise you one thing, and when you arrive they cheat you, take your passports and don't pay you the promised salary," confirms the head of the main administration for labor migration of the Tajik migration service, Tolib Shavripov.
Don't scold, boss!

Yet many citizens of the Central Asian republics who want to earn their money in Russia admit that they not only do not know the language of the destination country, but also have difficulty expressing themselves in writing in their own language.
Of course, it is not their fault, but rather the evil: few Turkmen, Uzbeks and Tajiks can afford even a basic education.
For in their families there is not even money to feed the children, let alone to buy them decent clothes, shoes and school supplies.
As teenagers, these children immediately take advantage of any opportunity to earn money.
"It is difficult without language skills", they admit.
"You feel humiliated and inferior."
Civil rights activists stress the following important aspect of the law.
The test must be taken only by migrants with legal status.
If you do not have this status, there is no examination and therefore no official work.
Meanwhile, the majority of the guest workers continue to live illegally in Russia.
"Welcome" or "Access for unauthorized persons prohibited"
Many migrants confirm that it is not easy to obtain an official status in Russia.
The reason is bureaucratic obstacles and, of course, the language difficulties.
It also costs money to legalize: 12 to 16 thousand rubles.
A fake registration can be made quickly and for only one thousand and five hundred.
Russian police officers know that our documents are mostly forged and that we are not registered, and this leads to cases of extortion.
"They want one or two hundred rubles for cigarettes and tea," says the Tajik Umed Huschkadamov to journalists.
"Don't be afraid to spend money on false papers"
As soon as the law came into force, it became clear that not only can the registration documents of migrants be forged.
Some fake certificates certifying that the language test has been passed have already been seized by officials of the Federal Migration Office.
The fake documents were printed on an ordinary color printer.
Of course, the new owners did not get the document for free: every migrant who hoped to avoid the tests paid seven thousand rubles for the document.
That is more than twice as much as the cost of the official test: it costs a migrant worker three thousand rubles.
As far as the most important immediate task is concerned, namely to protect the system from corruption so that certificates cannot be bought, both officials and civil rights activists agree.
For the moment, the authorities can only promise that they will provide time for a language course for those who fail the test the first time.
In addition, newcomers without language skills are offered jobs in areas where no active communication with people is required.
The Interior Ministry is ignoring the illegal arms trade
The proportion of legal weapons in crimes is extremely low
The Russian Interior Ministry is planning to tighten the law on private weapons ownership.
This is a response to recent events: the shooting at a wedding, the seven deaths in the shooting at the wedding of a lawyer, Dmitri Winogradov,
The police want to ban the carrying of non-lethal weapons in public and raise the age for the possession of firearms from 18 to 21.

The proposal has been supported by Irina Yarovaya, chairwoman of the Duma Committee on Security and Corruption, who has promised that the changes to the arms law will be presented to the Duma in the near future.
Not everyone is happy that the Russian authorities want to tackle the problems by "attracting the screws".
An open letter has been published on the Internet, in which representatives of various armed groups call on the authorities to refrain from "meaningless tightening up".
The percentage of crimes with registered weapons is very small, said the criminal lawyer , Vasily Lesnikov, to the Russian service of the BBC.

According to the Interior Ministry's statistics, 142 crimes involving the use of registered weapons were committed in the course of six months in 2012, while a total of 1,168 thousand offences were recorded during the same period.
The authors of the open letter are convinced that tightening the law on private firearms owners will not prevent criminals from using the black market.
At present, the authors claim that in Moscow you can find any weapon for a small amount of money.
Meanwhile, the Interior Ministry stresses that the circulation of illegal weapons is under control.
Suppliers: from the factories to the officers
The weapons are smuggled through several channels to the black market.
There are five such main channels, says a former colonel Viktor Baranez, who served for ten years in the Ministry of Education and in the General Staff.
Screenshot of a website accepting weapon orders
The first channel is the army, i. e. weapons stolen during the battles in the Caucasus.
"The weapons were stolen by both the Russian officers and the Caucasus themselves," says Baranez.
On the second channel, illegal weapons stolen from criminals are sold to police.
Baranez explains that these include weapons stolen from police armouries and directly from law enforcement officials.
Other illegal weapons come from military arsenals.
In many military camps there were frequent explosions.
"There is evidence that some of these cases were arson to conceal the lack of weapons," says the former military man.
A contribution to the black market is also made by the arms manufacturers, as Baranez has said.
"Today there are countless private arms factories that cannot compete with international competition and therefore sell their weapons on the black market, for example in Moscow," the expert reports.
Another channel of the black market is smuggling.
A large number of firearms come from poor countries such as Kyrgyzstan.
"There is a separate, sometimes artisanal production and a mafia that organizes smuggling," explains the former military man.
Where do the weapons come from?
Experts calculated the percentage of illegal weapons that each of the five channels supplies to the black market.
In 2011 a report was produced by the Centre for Problem Analysis and Public Administration.
The experts analyzed reports from the Ministry of the Interior and the Federal Service for State Statistics, criminological literature and publicly available data on weapons.
The overwhelming majority of illegal weapons, according to investigators, come from the army and the security forces.
Half of the weapons on the black market are there because of the "fault of people who have come into contact with weapons in their work", the report says.
According to the researchers, 17% of the weapons come from conflict zones, 14% are stolen from weapons factories, and 5% are from illegal excavations.
A sales representative of a gun shop, who does not want to be named, assures us that weapons found in illegal excavations are no longer sold because they are outdated.
According to him, it is more common for traders to obtain supplies from a weapons depot.
A weapon, for example a pistol of the type TT, is purchased from a flagman.
The weapon is issued and handed over through the fence.
"The dealer brings the weapon into the city and sells it there for €900 per piece with two magazines," he says

"The police of course knows everything and therefore, if it cannot carry out the plan to uncover crimes, it periodically carries out control purchases of dealers who offer illegal weapons," adds the sales representative.
"Like in a luxury shop"
Buyers and sellers most often find each other through friends.

I had looked at websites and blogs when someone called me and suggested that I should go to the station "Begowaja" where a person would be waiting for me to take me to a certain place where we would negotiate the price.
I found out the price of the weapon there
Military commentator Viktor Baranez
"To get a weapon, I need a friend who has contacts," says the salesman. "I have such a friend, but I do not trust him."
There are traders on the markets, but you have to go there and make an appointment with a code like "from Ivan Ivanovich, who says that the daughter has lost a tooth".
I am currently even getting through some of the rings through a friend whom I trust.
He supplies me with the rings because he knows that I will not condemn him.
Newcomers are looking for weapons in different ways.
Former military man Viktor Baranez tried his hand at buying illegal weapons in the mid-1990s, when he wrote an article on the subject.
The schemes have not changed, he says.
He received a photo album in which "anything and everything" was depicted.
"I felt like I was in a luxury shop," recalls the military man.
Baranez says that the buyer will not be buying a cat in a sack, but will be able to try everything out.
I as a potential customer do not just buy, but go into the forest with the seller, and there we set up a target.
"I can then shoot there, and if I am convinced that the gun is good, we negotiate with each other," the expert describes the procedure.
Shopping from the sofa
Internet search engines show search results for web pages and groups in "Vkontakte" where weapons are offered "for various purposes".
There is no need for any paperwork or personal meetings.
"You need only the right amount of money", reads the ad on the website "Buy a gun or rifle".
There users place their orders and make inquiries.
Is it sold to minors?
"Of course without a license", asks user "Ivan" (literal quote).
"Buy a TT. Moscow," is the laconic request of "Fedorenkov."
The Federal Security Service recently shut down countless fake websites, and buyers looking to purchase weapons are going online in droves.
People come in like hungry fish to be fed and then end up in Siberia to dig coal
Military commentator and former military officer Viktor Baranez
I have heard of the following scheme: the website is normally registered in a foreign country, and Russian law does not apply.
The responsible persons accept the orders.
The buyer transfers the money via an ATM.
